ideas.description: Instrument run with no recipe change, and the baseline for every following idea. The tip is E100 code (176e5ec). Its two distinct scored samples are 0.7561 and 0.7516, and its only off-seed sample is one process (22 seeds, 0.7523). E098 showed that one process per arm cannot resolve 0.1 pp. In an untimed side script, run the unchanged E100 code through the benchmark's own trial code on seeds 3-26 in 2 more fresh processes, so cuDNN picks are resampled. Do not edit benchmark/. Log per-seed accuracy, per-seed final-weight checksums and the cuDNN conv kernel names per (layer, shape); the kernel names are the free by-product for H4.5.1. For the scored row, rerun E100 unchanged; a non-bit-identical result adds a third distinct scored sample. Store the pooled 24-seed vectors (>=2 distinct processes) as the paired baseline for every later off-seed A/B.
ideas.expected: Time ~4.46 s (±0.5%). Scored accuracy 0.751-0.756. Pooled off-seed mean for E100 0.7518-0.7530, with process-to-process sd of the 24-seed mean ~0.05-0.12 pp. If the pooled distinct scored mean (3 samples) is >=0.7535, E100 counts as robustly banked. If it is <0.7530, E100 is feasible by luck like E090, and the next zero-time accuracy lever must land before any time cut. If kernel-name sets cluster with process means (>=0.2 pp apart), H4.5.1 is supported.

ideas.description: Placement-paired test of the path-length mechanism in the low-res phases. E104 bought ~+0.12 pp off-seed by running the 16/24 px phases at bs 1024, i.e. ~1.5x more Muon steps there, at +2.8% time. If the gain is Muon path length (lr × steps) rather than update count, a 1.5x larger Muon lr in those phases should reproduce it at zero time. Base: E100 code. In the 16 and 24 px phases only (bs 1536, warmup included), multiply the conv-filter Muon lr schedule by 1.5 (0.24 -> 0.36 at the same schedule position). The head keeps its 0.5x multiplier and scales along. The SGD groups, the 28/32 px phases (32 px keeps its 1.25x) and the tail are unchanged. Implement it as a phase-keyed host-side factor written into the existing 0-d lr tensor, so nothing recompiles. Before scoring, smoke-test that the 16 px loss stays finite over the first 30 steps. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=2 fresh processes, paired against the E100 baseline, plus two distinct scored samples.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, ~4.46 s). Path-length prediction: off-seed +0.06 to +0.12 pp over E100, i.e. most of E104's gain for free. If it passes (pooled off-seed >= +0.08 pp and a distinct scored mean >=0.7540), it becomes the tip and funds a ~1-1.5% 32 px trim. If the gain is <= +0.03 pp, E104's gain was update count, and only the per-step-cost batch route remains. A loss of >=0.1 pp means early Muon steps are already at the stability edge (the 64x-LR SGD biases are not touched, so the loss would be attributable to the filters).

ideas.description: Dose-response on the one weakly supported zero-time lever. E100 multiplied the 32 px-phase filter Muon lr by 1.25 (+0.09 pp off-seed, distinct scored mean 0.7538). Base: E100 code. Change only that 32 px-phase factor, from 1.25 to 1.5 (0.36 at the same schedule position; the floor-hold covers the same samples, at 1.5x). The head keeps 0.5x and scales along. Nothing else changes, and the phase-keyed 0-d tensor means nothing recompiles. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=2 fresh processes against the E100 baseline, plus two distinct scored samples.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). If path length is still below its optimum, off-seed +0.04 to +0.10 pp over E100, and the factor becomes the tip setting. If the result is within ±0.04 pp, the optimum is near 1.25-1.5, so keep 1.25 (simpler). If it is <= -0.08 pp, 1.25 was at or past the optimum, and E100's gain might partly be noise; H10.2 confidence then drops. Dose-response monotonicity (1.0 -> 1.25 -> 1.5) is the key evidence for the mechanism.

ideas.description: Extend E100's path-length factor to the other bs-1024 phase. In E100 only the 32 px phase got the 1.25x Muon lr. The 1.25-epoch 28 px phase also runs at bs 1024 and is part of the late, test-adjacent training that H11 calls binding. Base: E100 code. In the 28 px phase only, multiply the conv-filter Muon lr schedule by 1.25. The head scales along. The 16/24 px phases, the 32 px factor (1.25) and the tail are unchanged. This is a phase-keyed host-side factor, so nothing recompiles. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=2 fresh processes against the E100 baseline, plus two distinct scored samples. If the low-res-lr idea (H10.2) passes first, rebase onto it.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Prediction: off-seed +0.03 to +0.08 pp, smaller than E100's +0.09 because the 28 px phase has fewer samples than the 32 px phase. A pass (>= +0.06 pp off-seed with distinct scored mean >= base) makes it the tip setting. A result within ±0.04 pp means the late gain is specific to the 32 px phase, which supports H11's test-resolution exposure over generic late path length.

ideas.description: Explore H11's mechanism (b): late training on test-like inputs is what binds. Base: E100 code. For the last ~12% of samples (inside the 32 px phase, covering the floor-hold and final EMA), turn off the translate-2 augmentation, keeping the alternating flip, so late training sees un-shifted 32 px images like the test set. This is a host-side flag in the GPU augmentation; the net graph is unchanged, and if the augment op is compiled, warm both variants in build. E008 showed short schedules under-fit, so less late augmentation may help. Change nothing else. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26 in >=2 fresh processes against the E100 baseline, plus one scored sample and a second only if off-seed >= +0.05 pp.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged or -0.1% (one fewer gather in late batches). Accuracy -0.1 to +0.12 pp. If off-seed is >= +0.08 pp, late augmentation annealing is a free margin source and H11(b) gains support; the next step is tuning the anneal point (8-20%). If off-seed is <= -0.08 pp, translate regularization still matters at the end (consistent with LS 0.3 being optimal), and this line closes.

ideas.description: Free, untimed analysis with no scored-path change. The judge is a 300 W A100 PCIe. Using existing NVML/phase logs (E045 onward; add a short NVML capture in the E100 rerun if the logs lack per-phase energy), project the judge time of E095, E090/E096 and E100 as the sum over phases of max(phase energy / 300 W, phase GPU-busy time). Also project the two depth-cut variants once I114 has measured them. Report the projected ranking and the gap ratios against the local times. For the scored row, if one is required, rerun E100 unchanged (an extra distinct sample).
ideas.expected: No time or accuracy change (scored row ~4.46 s, 0.751-0.756). Prediction: projected PCIe times are ~1.15-1.3x local, and the E095-vs-E100 gap widens by >=1.1x, because the extra 32 px work is energy-bound. Use the projection only to break ties between configs within 3% locally. Depth cuts, as FLOP and byte levers, should project at least as well as they measure locally.

drop.reason: Stale base: it targets E090. The tip is now E100, where the 32 px phase already runs at 1.25x Muon lr (0.30), so 'lr 0.28 everywhere' is confounded with E100's change. The remaining parts of H7.1.3 (raising lr in the 16/24/28 px phases) are re-proposed on E100 as the phase-specific H10.2 ideas, which also test a mechanism.

The tip is E100 (E096 plus 1.25x Muon lr in the 32 px phase): ~4.46 s, distinct scored mean 0.7538, and only one off-seed process. Two things are settled. Extra Muon updates buy accuracy at about the same rate wherever they go, ~0.04 pp per 1% of time (E084/E095/E104), which is no better than the 32 px trims they would fund. End-of-run averaging, the whitening-bias window and cudnn.benchmark_limit are closed (E099/E102/E103). That leaves two routes to a faster robust tip: zero-time accuracy that lets the 32 px phase shrink, and depth cuts.

**New queue (6 new ideas plus I114):**
1. **Confirm E100 (priority 4).** Rerun it unchanged in 2 more fresh processes on seeds 3-26, plus a scored rerun. This decides whether E100 is robustly feasible and gives the paired baseline for the ideas below.
2. **Higher Muon lr in the low-res phases (priority 4, H10.2).** Multiply the Muon lr by 1.5x in the 16/24 px phases only. If E104's +0.12 pp came from Muon path length (lr × steps) rather than from the extra steps themselves, this gets most of it at zero time cost.
3. **Dose-response at 32 px (priority 3, H10.2.1).** Raise E100's 32 px factor from 1.25x to 1.5x. A steady rise from 1.0 to 1.25 to 1.5 would be the strongest evidence that path length is the mechanism.
4. **Extend 1.25x to the 28 px phase (priority 3, H10.2).** This separates "late training generally benefits" from "only the 32 px phase benefits" (H11).
5. **Turn off translate-2 for the last ~12% of samples (priority 2, explore, H11).** This tests whether late training on test-like inputs is what limits accuracy.
6. **Project times for the 300 W PCIe judge from existing power logs (priority 1, free).** Used only to break ties between configs within 3% of each other locally.

I114 (profile the two depth cuts before any scored run) stays queued as the main remaining time lever.

**Dropped:** I105. It targets the old E090 base and is confounded with E100's lr change; its remaining question is covered by the phase-specific lr ideas above.

**Decision rule for every A/B:** at least 2 fresh processes per arm, compared seed-for-seed against E100 on seeds 3-26, plus distinct scored samples (the E098 lesson that one process cannot resolve 0.1 pp).
